Nine people are dead and 15 injured after a Polish gunman launched a series of assaults in the southern city of Krakow, leading authorities to declare it a terrorist attack motivated by extremist right-wing views.

The man is suspected of killing three people in his family home before driving to the historic square in central Krakow and opening fire on the crowd during a busy Saturday afternoon.

Police responded within minutes by wounding the shooter and detaining him, but the assault left two officers wounded and one of them was described as fighting for his life.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the attacks as terrorism and said the country had not seen such a drastic terror attack before.

Tusk named the officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur Morański, calling them heroes.

“They likely saved many lives, without regard for the risk of losing their own. Their condition is serious, but they are receiving excellent care,” he said.

The bodies of two women and a man were found at the home of the gunman after he had been detained, Tusk told reporters at a press conference on Saturday night (early Sunday, AEDT).

The final attack took place in the city’s Main Square, one of the most-visited locations in the city in the heart of the Old Town.

The gunman, 25, drove to multiple locations in the pedestrian square and opened fire at each stop with an automatic weapon, killing four women and two men.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the man held “very radical” and “ultranationalistic” views, but authorities did not release his name.

“Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” Kierwiński said at a news conference.

The police said a British national was among those killed and five foreign nationals were among the wounded.

Those injured in the attack include three police officers.
